name: CoolIT Systems Inc.
headquarters: #200, 115 Quarry Park Road SE, Calgary, Alberta T2C 5G9, Canada (Starfield manufacturing and Liquid Lab also in Calgary; Taipei Liquid Lab; offices in Wilmington DE, Shenzhen and Abu Dhabi)
employees: 'approximately 363 employees as at December 31, 2024' (statutory forced-labour report); about 650 at the March 2026 sale to Ecolab (KKR and Ecolab materials, Calgary Herald); 'nearly 900' by August 2026 (Calgary Herald)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: CoolIT Systems is the Calgary direct-liquid-cooling specialist that Ecolab bought from KKR for about USD 4.75 billion in cash on 2 July 2026 — 29 times estimated next-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA on roughly USD 550 million of expected sales — because it sits at every point where liquid touches an AI rack: the cold plate on the GPU, the manifold in the rack, the coolant distribution unit (CDU) in the row, and the pre-fabricated piping between them; its CHx2000 row CDU is rated at 2,000 kW and twelve NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 racks, it manufactures 'multi-gigawatts' of CDU capacity a year in Canada, China and Vietnam, and a CDU for racks above 1 MW is due on 28 September 2026. BACKGROUND. Incorporated 27 February 2001 by Alexander 'Sandy' Scott, Brydon Gierl and Jason Myers; started in gaming-PC liquid coolers, shipped its first Xeon cold plate in 2013, and has been factory-installed in Dell PowerEdge servers since 2017 (company history). Direct liquid cooling by CoolIT is in 'seven of the top 10 supercomputers' including El Capitan, the TOP500 No. 1 of November 2024; the company claims '5+ million cold plates shipped', deployments at '300+ data centers' in more than 80 countries, and '4 of the top 5 server OEMs and 4 of the 5 hyperscalers as customers' — no hyperscaler is named anywhere. KKR's Global Impact Fund II bought a majority in May 2023 (value undisclosed; the Calgary Herald reports US$270 million) with Mubadala as minority co-investor; under that ownership CDU capacity rose 25-fold, headcount roughly doubled and, per KKR's exit materials, revenue was on track to quadruple with EBITDA up tenfold through 2026. The sale to Ecolab was agreed on 20 March 2026 and closed early; CoolIT now reports inside Ecolab's Global Water segment, and Ecolab has set a USD 4 billion, 25-percent-margin target for its Global High-Tech business by 2030. Two premises in the commissioning brief did not survive research and are corrected here rather than smoothed: CoolIT is Ecolab-owned, not KKR-owned; and the Asetek patent litigation never produced a jury verdict — the 2019 case ended on an 11 September 2022 summary judgment holding Asetek's last live patent valid but not infringed by any CoolIT product, followed by a confidential settlement and dismissal with prejudice on 6 October 2022, with CoolIT's own '567 patent later revived by the Federal Circuit in March 2024. Collection gap, stated: CoolIT publishes no revenue, margin, installed-megawatt or annual unit figure of its own; every financial number here is the acquirer's. The two Asian contract manufacturers are unnamed; CDU weights, heat-exchanger type and coolant temperature limits beyond the ASHRAE class are not published; and no customer in this corpus is named by either side.
ecosystemRole: The CDU specialist the corpus lacked: where Vertiv, Schneider Electric (through Motivair) and Trane (through LiquidStack) reach liquid cooling from the plant side, CoolIT reaches it from the chip — it designs the cold plate to the silicon vendor's reference (NVIDIA's Recommended Vendor List; Intel and AMD series), builds the loop and the manifold for the server OEM (Dell, HPE, Gigabyte; Supermicro as a stated collaborator), and sells the row and in-rack CDUs that separate that clean technology-cooling loop from the building's water. Its counterparties in this corpus are therefore NVIDIA on the design side and Vertiv and Schneider on the competitive side; its customers — 'four of the five hyperscalers' — are unnamed. Since July 2026 it is also the hardware half of Ecolab's water-and-chemistry pitch to data centres, with coolant monitoring (3D TRASAR) and on-site service bundled to the CDU.

productsAndServices.name: Row-based liquid-to-liquid CDUs — CHx2000, CHx1500, CHx500 (and the legacy CHx750)
productsAndServices.category: Coolant distribution units — row / megawatt class
productsAndServices.description: Free-standing liquid-to-liquid coolant distribution units in a 750 × 1,200 mm rack footprint that isolate the technology cooling system (TCS) from the facility water system (FWS) through an internal heat exchanger, pump treated coolant to a row of racks, filter it, and report through Redfish, SNMP, Modbus and BACnet with group control of up to 20 units.
highlights: CHx2000 — 'The AI CDU': '2000 kW cooling capacity at 5°C ATD' (approach temperature differential), '2125 LPM at 35 psi', power consumption '12.24 kW', '12 x GB300 NVL72 racks per CDU', 'best-in-class performance density (1698 kW/m²)', 'All stainless-steel piping', '4" tri-clamp interface at facility water system (FWS) and technology cooling system (TCS)', '100% PG25 leak testing for every unit', production '100 units per week' — in production since October 2024 (product page and sheet, 2026).

Launch framing (April 2025): 'CHx2000 offers an unrivaled 2 MW liquid cooling capacity. With a flow rate of 1.2 liters per minute per kilowatt (LPM/kW), it supports cooling for up to twelve 120kW NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 racks'; 'over 2X cooling capacity than the next best 1350 CDU and unmatched 53 psi secondary head pressure'; 'integrated 25-micron filtration'; 'Built-in redundancies and group control for up to 20 units enable six-nines (99.9999%) availability'.

CHx1500: '1500 kW at 5°C approach temperature (2100 LPM primary, 1800 LPM secondary, PG25 coolant)'; 'Delivers 1500 LPM at 34 psi external pressure drop in single pump operation (N+N pump redundancy)'; 'Built-in 25 µ filters with 50 µ option'; 'Integrated ultracapacitor for interruption-free operation … Optional ATS'; 'Compatible with ASHRAE W+'; 'can cool 9 x NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 racks today' (brochure and March 2025 release).

CHx500 (announced July 2024): 'Four CHx500 units can be stacked to provide an unprecedented 2 MW of heat management in a single rack', 'Supporting ASHRAE W45 cooling'; no live product page in 2026. CHx750 (legacy): nine units managed 5.5 MW across 91 racks at TACC's Frontera; three cool GWDG's Emmy at 32 °C inlet with a DLC PUE of 1.07.

The company's own selection rule: 'A target of 1.5 liters per minute (LPM) per kilowatt (kW) of heat is typical for AI systems'; 'A lower approach temperature (the delta between facility supply fluid and technical fluid) indicates better cooling performance'; 'Look for internal redundancy in pumps, filters, sensors, and power supplies' (January 2026).

Next generation: 'Launching September 28, 2026: CoolIT's next-generation CDU is engineered for 1MW+ ultra-dense AI racks' — no name, capacity or specification disclosed; the company's own blog says 'Liquid-to-liquid CDUs rated in the multi-megawatt range will be necessary to support 1MW+ racks'.
productsAndServices.positioning: Against Vertiv (which Dell'Oro names as market leader), Motivair (Schneider Electric), Boyd, nVent and roughly forty other CDU vendors, CoolIT's published comparison puts the CHx2000 at 2,269 kW cooling load against anonymised competitors' 1,073 kW and 734 kW, on the same footprint; HPE specifies a 1.3 MW in-row CDU for eight GB200/GB300 racks. Dell'Oro (September 2025): 'Established names such as Vertiv, CoolIT, or Boyd will need to maintain their edge' and 'We expect fewer than 10 vendors to ultimately capture the lion's share of the market.'
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct to hyperscalers and colocation operators, through server OEMs and ODMs as part of a rack-scale solution, and via NVIDIA's Recommended Vendor List to NVIDIA's manufacturing partners; skidded CDUs built to order — 'one large cloud service provider requested thousands of skidded CDUs'.
targetSegments: Server OEMs and ODMs integrating rack-scale DLC
productsAndServices.roadmap: A multi-megawatt-class CDU for 1 MW+ racks launching 28 September 2026 (announced 2026-08-17); 'System-level designs that enable future >1MW rack power' (June 2026 tech brief).

productsAndServices.name: Liquid-to-air CDUs — AHx240 and AHx180
productsAndServices.description: CDUs that reject the technology-loop heat to the room's air through an internal radiator and fan array, so that direct-liquid-cooled racks can be deployed in air-cooled data centres with no facility water — the retrofit and bridging form factor.
highlights: AHx240: 'The highest-capacity liquid-to-air CDU for the latest AI deployments in traditional air-cooled data centers'; 'No facility water required'; cooling capacity '240 kW'; '2x GB300/GB200 NVL72 racks per CDU (at 15°C ATD and N+1 pump redundancy)'; '280LPM at 35psi'; power consumption '15.5 kW'; 'N+N redundancy on all critical components'; '8-Fan Array'; 2,293 × 1,200 × 1,199 mm; '100 units per week production capacities' (product page and sheet, 2026). At launch in July 2024 the company said one unit 'can cool up to four [NVIDIA GB200] NVL72 racks'; the 2026 page says two GB300 racks at 15 °C approach — the same box re-rated to a hotter chip.

AHx180: '180 kW cooling capacity at 15°C approach'; '2 x high-performance pumps', '4 x high-efficiency fans'; 'Delivers 270 LPM at a 40 psi external pressure drop under single-pump operation'; 'Integrated 50 µ serviceable filter with 25 µ to 150 µ options'; 'Redundant pumps (2N) and fan (N+1)'; 'Integrated sensors: flow, pressure, temperature, humidity, coolant level and leak detection'; power consumption '11.32 kW'; 'Supports common hot and cold aisle data center architecture'; 'Up to 2 NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 racks'.

The trade-off in the company's and the standards body's words: liquid-to-air keeps DLC out of the facility's plumbing but hands the heat back to the CRAH; ASHRAE notes that 'liquid/air heat exchangers have much higher approach temperatures than liquid/liquid' — hence the 15 °C rating basis against 5 °C for the CHx line.
Dell'Oro (September 2025): 'L2A CDUs have maintained a role even with large operators—ideal for retrofit projects'.
productsAndServices.positioning: Vertiv and Motivair sell liquid-to-air units too; CoolIT's claim is highest capacity in the class and OEM validation across NVIDIA racks. The form factor's ceiling is the room's air-handling capacity, not the CDU.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Same channels as the CHx line; positioned for retrofit of existing air-cooled halls and for early GB200 deployments where facility water is not yet plumbed.
targetSegments: Enterprises and colocation operators retrofitting air-cooled halls
Early AI deployments awaiting facility-water build-out
Edge and HPC sites without chilled-water loops

productsAndServices.name: In-rack CDUs — CHx200 and CHx80
productsAndServices.description: Four-rack-unit liquid-to-liquid CDUs mounted at the top or bottom of a single rack, giving each cabinet its own isolated technology loop.
highlights: CHx200: 'Capable of managing 200 kW of heat load in a remarkably small 4U of space, this system provides cooling for up to 200 servers'; 'Compatible with ASHRAE W17 to W+ warm water cooling'; 'N+1 redundant pumps and power supplies'; 'Intelligent controls with leak detection'; 'Servers remain hot-swappable for service'. First field installation TU Dresden's Birdie (2019); 26 units at CHIME; four at amplitUDE (2024).
CHx80: '80 kW of heat load in a remarkably small 4U of space … cooling for up to 100 servers'; otherwise identical feature set; used in Dell's Zenith innovation-lab cluster.

The architecture argument, from an analyst rather than the vendor: in-rack CDUs' 'Slightly lower partial power usage effectiveness (pPUE) can be offset by advantages in modularity, ease of off-site rack integration and commissioning, and containment of faults and leaks' (Dell'Oro, September 2025); Vertiv's own guidance notes the form factor 'reduces the impact of potential cooling outages to one rack instead of multiple … but adds mechanical complexity inside the rack'.
Flow, pressure, filtration and power figures for the 4U units are not published — a gap the datasheet-first buyer should note.
productsAndServices.positioning: A mature line (2019 first install) now secondary to the row CDUs for AI; competes with Vertiv's and Motivair's rack CDUs and with the in-house rack CDUs Supermicro and Lenovo build.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Through OEM rack-scale integrations and direct.

productsAndServices.name: Cold plates and coldplate loops — Split-Flow, OMNI, the 4 kW and 15 kW demonstrators
productsAndServices.description: Copper microchannel cold plates bolted to CPUs, GPUs, accelerators, memory, optics, storage and power components, assembled into server loops with chassis manifolds and quick disconnects; designed per silicon vendor and per OEM board layout, manufactured at clean-room lines in Canada, China and Vietnam.
highlights: Split-Flow (patented 2009): 'CoolIT's patented micro-channel architecture. In addition to up to 30% better coolant flow and heat capture versus standard coldplates, the Split-Flow design directs coolant to a chip's hotspot to ensure uniform cooling'; 'drastically reduces internal pressure drop'.

OMNI all-metal cold plate (May 2024): 'aerospace-grade all-metallic unibody construction, OMNI Coldplates eliminate the risk of differential coefficients of thermal expansion (CTE) from using multiple materials'; handles 'thermal loads exceeding 1,500 W TDP and thermal fluxes over 300 W/cm2' with 'up to 60% lower thermal resistance compared with standard coldplates'; launch SKUs for NVIDIA GB200, H100, GH200, Intel Data Center Max and Xeon, and AMD.

4,000 W demonstrator (March 2025): 'capturing 97%+ of heat from a 4000W thermal test vehicle (TTV) with a flow rate of 6 litres per minute (LPM)' — 'equivalent to 1.5 LPM per kW' — with 'ultra-low thermal resistance of Tr<0.009 C/W while limiting the full flow loop pressure drop (including all fittings and QDs) to just 8 PSI'.

15 kW demonstrator (June 2026): 'validated with a standard water-glycol coolant at 1.2 L/min/kW' and 'suitable for 45°C warm-water cooling environments'; the tech brief ran three cold plates on a 15 kW test vehicle at 45 °C inlet with an average coolant temperature rise 'just below 35°C' and 'an average case temperature (Tcase) of 80°C' — the company's answer to the claim that single-phase DLC tops out at '2 to 2.5 kW' per device.

Product series: CP-NV-GB200-SUPERCHIP (Grace Blackwell and Blackwell Ultra), CP-NV-B200-GPU, CP-NV-GH200-SUPERCHIP, CP-NV-H200-GPU; CP-AMD-MI355-GPU, MI300X, MI300A, MI250, SP7 (Venice), SP5, SP3; CP-INT-SR-CPU, CP-INT-GR-CPU; CP-OSFP, CP-DDR5-DIMM, CP-DDR4-DIMM 'enable 100% heat capture across the server'. The NA2 loop for NVIDIA GB200 is catalogued by part number (900-02162 to 900-02165).

Scale: '5+ million cold plates shipped'; '10,000s of server coldplate loops per month'; loops 'from 70% to 100% Heat Capture' enabling 'Fanless Designs'; 'more than 150 liquid cooling patents' (July 2026; earlier pages say 100-plus and 120-plus).
productsAndServices.positioning: The cold plate is where the Asetek dispute was fought and where Supermicro and Lenovo build in-house; CoolIT's claim is thermal headroom (4 kW and 15 kW demonstrated on single-phase water-glycol) that pushes back two-phase and immersion alternatives. Dell'Oro: 'Single-phase direct liquid cooling accounts for the vast majority of liquid-cooled capacity coming online today'.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Designed into OEM and ODM servers (Dell factory-installed since 2017; HPE Cray EX and Apollo; Gigabyte; Supermicro as stated collaborator) and co-developed with hyperscalers — 'CoolIT partners with hyperscalers to co-develop and mass produce coldplates, loops, rack manifolds and CDUs'.
productsAndServices.roadmap: 'New coldplate architecture, including direct-to-die and micro-channel lids' (June 2026 tech brief).

productsAndServices.name: Rack manifolds, quick disconnects and prefabricated technology-cooling-system piping
productsAndServices.description: Stainless-steel vertical rack manifolds in EIA, ORV3 and MGX rack series with dry-break quick disconnects, and prefabricated TCS piping — stainless with Victaulic couplings or polypropylene (Aquatherm) — connecting CDUs to rows of racks.
highlights: Manifolds: 'EIA racks: 42U, 48U, 52U', 'ORV3 racks: 44OU', custom heights; 'Corrosion-resistant treated stainless steel construction'; 'Industry-leading all-metal dry-break quick disconnects available from multiple trusted suppliers'; 'FD83 quick-disconnect connectors are the most commonly used TCS connection type in production deployments'; '100% leak testing before it ships (including the quick-disconnect fittings) under both static and dynamic conditions'; 'hardware-agnostic … work with any CDU and any liquid-cooled server platform'.
Quality control on the connector: 'AI-based high-speed optical screening confirms O-ring presence on every Quick Disconnect before installation on our Vertical Rack Manifolds' (December 2025).

TCS piping: 'SAE 304 or 316 stainless steel with polished option', '2.5" to 8" piping options', 'Modules undergo passivation and pickling processes before shipping to site', or 'Prefabricated modular Aquatherm components fused onsite' in polypropylene to 'Prevent galvanic reactions and corrosion'; optional loop telemetry to the BMS.

Why prefabrication: OCP's cloud-scale TCS guidance notes that 'Achieving stringent filtration requirements, such as 25 microns, is challenging with conventional job-site construction, as materials like pipe tape and pipe dope are prohibited within TCS systems'; CoolIT's answer is to 'shift critical assembly activities into a controlled manufacturing environment'.
productsAndServices.positioning: Competes with Victaulic-based mechanical contractors and the OEMs' own manifolds; the value is the leak-tested, pre-cleaned assembly arriving as one part number.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: With the CDU as a system, or standalone to any platform.
targetSegments: Hyperscalers standardising on ORV3 or MGX

productsAndServices.name: Global professional services, coolant and Ecolab-integrated monitoring
productsAndServices.description: Site survey, system flush and fill, CDU commissioning, factory witness testing on a 6 MW rig, planned preventive maintenance with coolant analysis, service-level agreements, and — since the Ecolab acquisition — continuous coolant monitoring.
highlights: Coolant: 'CoolIT uses a Propylene Glycol 25% computer coolant mixture, consisting of additional inhibitors to reduce corrosion and microbial growth'; PG25 is the factory fill and leak-test fluid across the line; 'It's not just water; we use fluids like PG25 or LC25, and compatibility matters' (director of professional services, November 2025).

Maintenance: 'Planned Preventative Maintenance (PPM) visits are typically scheduled every 6 months' with 'coolant sampling and coolant analysis to ensure the integrity of the fluid'; 'Service Level Agreements range from 2-5 years in 1 year increments'; support 'in over 80 countries'.
Field lesson the company tells against itself: 'We worked with a hyperscaler where we discovered their flushing procedures weren't adequate. Filters were clogging within minutes.'

Ecolab: 'CoolIT's preventive on-site maintenance programs, along with continuous coolant monitoring with the Ecolab™ 3D TRASAR™ system, provide an additional level of assurance' (June 2026); Ecolab's own thesis — 'bringing together CoolIT's engineered cooling technologies with Ecolab's expertise in water, chemistry and digital service'.

Test capacity: 'Boilers and cooling towers supporting up to 6 MW of simulated load'; '18 thermal chambers, a 1MW data center simulator'; in-house UL-DAP capability; erosion research on the 1.5 m/s copper velocity limit with PG25 (May 2025).
productsAndServices.positioning: The recurring-revenue layer Ecolab paid for: chemistry, monitoring and service around hardware that competitors sell as one-time equipment.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: SLAs attached to CDU sales; Ecolab's field-service organisation post-close.

recentDevelopments.read: An answer to the two-phase and immersion camps: single-phase water-glycol has headroom to the 2030 chip roadmap.

recentDevelopments.headline: Calgary Herald's inside story of the sale: incorporated 27 February 2001 by Sandy Scott, Brydon Gierl and Jason Myers; KKR's 2023 purchase reported at US$270 million; employee payouts from one year's salary to eight times annual wage, averaging $240,000
recentDevelopments.read: A US$270 million entry and a US$4.75 billion exit in three years is the return that will bring every private-equity buyer to the next liquid-cooling specialist.

recentDevelopments.headline: Mubadala agrees to sell its minority stake in the KKR-led USD 4.75 billion transaction; under their ownership CoolIT 'increased coolant distribution unit (CDU) capacity by 25x' and 'delivered approximately 2.18 billion kWh in energy savings in 2025'

recentDevelopments.read: The only growth-rate statements in the record are the seller's; they imply a business whose EBITDA margin expanded sharply as it scaled.

recentDevelopments.headline: Financial Times reports KKR working with advisers on a sale of CoolIT 'for a price tag potentially exceeding $3 billion'

recentDevelopments.read: The only volume figures the company publishes, and they are monthly orders of magnitude rather than counts.

recentDevelopments.headline: Federal Circuit vacates and remands the PTAB's unpatentability finding on CoolIT's US 9,057,567 cold-plate patent, construing 'matingly engaged' as 'mechanically joined or fitted together' — the last act of a twelve-year dispute with Asetek that ended in the district court with an 11 September 2022 summary judgment of non-infringement for all CoolIT products and a confidential settlement on 6 October 2022

relationships.via: NVIDIA Partner Network; Recommended Vendor List
relationships.note: Member of the NVIDIA Partner Network as 'a Solution Advisor for Compute and DGX AI Compute Systems' with cold plates, manifolds and CDUs on NVIDIA's Recommended Vendor List; NVIDIA engineers are quoted endorsing CoolIT in 2024 and, with Ecolab, in 2026.
relationships.context:
CoolIT's collaboration with NVIDIA 'began in 2009 with the design of the NV200 VGA coldplate for the GeForce GTX 295'. In October 2024 it joined the NVIDIA Partner Network for the Blackwell ramp; NVIDIA's Jeremy Rodriguez, senior director of data center engineering, said the expansion 'will help meet the growing demands of data centers'. At GTC 2025 the company stated that all its chip-to-CDU products 'are available to NVIDIA's server manufacturing partners through the NVIDIA Recommended Vendor List (RVL)', and its site tabulates GB200 NVL72 racks per CDU (CHx2000 12, CHx1500 9, AHx240 4, AHx180 2).

At the Ecolab close NVIDIA's Ali Heydari and Saket Karajgikar stated that 'NVIDIA has collaborated with Ecolab and CoolIT across a broad range of liquid-cooling initiatives, including coolant qualification, coolant health monitoring, cooling infrastructure development, and next-generation AI factory technologies'. No formal 'NVIDIA-certified' or reference-design designation exists; no CoolIT product is claimed for Vera Rubin NVL72.

relationships.note: Dell'Oro names Vertiv as 'leading the liquid cooling market' with CoolIT among the 'established players … maintaining strong market share positions'.
relationships.context: Dell'Oro's January 2026 release: 'The competitive landscape is evolving rapidly, with Vertiv leading the liquid cooling market and established players such as CoolIT, nVent, and Boyd maintaining strong market share positions.' Its September 2025 CDU note records 'Vertiv's acquisition of CoolTera in December 2023' and expects 'fewer than 10 vendors to ultimately capture the lion's share'. Omdia's June 2024 release had placed CoolIT first in a roughly USD 1 billion 2023 market. Vertiv reaches liquid cooling from the plant and power side; CoolIT from the chip.

relationships.note: Schneider Electric entered the CDU market through its October 2024 purchase of Motivair, which Gigabyte lists alongside CoolIT as a direct-liquid-cooling partner.
relationships.context: Dell'Oro's CDU analysis cites 'Schneider Electric's purchase of Motivair in October 2024' among the consolidation moves reshaping the category. Giga Computing's 2023 release put the two head to head: 'Motivair joins our other partner, CoolIT Systems, to demonstrate GIGABYTE's dedication to offering a comprehensive DLC solution'. Schneider's own CDU guidance (five CDU functions; rack-mounted units 20 to about 40 kW) is the teaching text quoted in this dossier's study guide.

policyExposure.exposure: CoolIT files the statutory report (CIT-RPT-002, signed by the CEO on 30 May 2025): it 'meets the definition of an entity', employs 'more than 250 employees globally' and 'utilizes two principal third-party contract manufacturers based in Shenzhen, China, and Vietnam who either ship parts to Calgary for assembly or function as original equipment manufacturers'; component sourcing spans twenty countries including China, Malaysia, Taiwan and the United States. The report is also the only first-party headcount ('approximately 363 employees as at December 31, 2024') and the only named description of the Asian manufacturing footprint.
policyExposure.mitigation: Vendor Code of Conduct aligned to SA8000; supplier qualification questionnaire; an ESG assessment by ERM Inc. in late 2023; Tier-2 supplier mapping planned for 2025; 'zero incidents' reported.

policyExposure.regime: US–Canada trade measures (Section 232 and reciprocal tariffs)
policyExposure.exposure: CoolIT makes no first-party statement on tariffs. Its exposure is structural: CDUs are 'Produced in volume … at CoolIT's Canadian manufacturing operations' for a customer base that is largely American, with cold-plate loops built in China and Vietnam. The statutory report records that '2024 was dedicated to evaluating geopolitical risks, trade restrictions, and economic trends that may impact vendor reliability and sourcing strategies' and that 'In 2024, CIT continued taking steps to shift critical component suppliers to North America', naming Wieland and Stoltz as near-shored vendors.
policyExposure.mitigation: Stated: dual sourcing and geographic diversification of suppliers ('CoolIT dual-sources key components and diversifies supplier geographies'); the acquirer plans new US offices in the Bay Area and Houston but no US manufacturing plant is reported.

policyExposure.exposure: The industry's temperature vocabulary for facility water: the 2021 fifth edition renamed the classes by their upper limit — 'W17 (previously W1), W27 (W2), W32 (W3), W40 (new), W45 (W4), and W+ (W5)' with 'a lower temperature limit of 2°C'. CoolIT rates the CHx200 and CHx80 'Compatible with ASHRAE W17 to W+', the CHx1500 'Compatible with ASHRAE W+', the CHx500 for 'ASHRAE W45', and validated its 15 kW cold plate at 45 °C inlet; every rating that decides whether a site can run without a chiller is written in these classes.
policyExposure.mitigation: The company's own position is that warm-water classes reduce but do not remove mechanical cooling ('it's not chiller-free', January 2026).

policyExposure.regime: Open Compute Project — ORV3 racks and Modular TCS guidance
policyExposure.exposure: Rack manifolds are offered in an 'ORV3 Rack Series' ('ORV3 racks: 44OU') alongside EIA and MGX; the CEO was 'a founding board member of the Open Compute Project' with '9+ years on the board'. OCP's cloud-scale TCS guidance sets the filtration and construction expectations (25 µm inline plus sidestream filtration; no pipe tape or dope in the TCS) that CoolIT's prefabricated piping and 25-micron CDU filtration are built to meet. No OCP specification authored by CoolIT was found.

policyExposure.regime: US patent law — inter partes review and district-court enforcement (Asetek dispute)
policyExposure.exposure: Twelve years of litigation with Asetek over sealed-loop and cold-plate patents (N.D. Cal. 2012; N.D. Cal. and D. Del. 2014; N.D. Cal. 2019–2022; PTAB and Federal Circuit 2020–2024). The 2019 case ended when Judge Chen 'GRANTS IN PART CoolIT's Motion for summary judgment with regards to noninfringement of the reservoir and curved blade limitations of Asetek's '362 Patent' while holding that patent valid; the parties then settled on confidential terms and the case was dismissed with prejudice on 6 October 2022. The Federal Circuit later vacated the PTAB's unpatentability finding on CoolIT's '567 patent (7 March 2024). No damages were awarded to either side in any of the actions.
policyExposure.mitigation: CoolIT's stated position (October 2022): the court 'granted summary judgment of non-infringement for all of CoolIT's past and current products in regard to Asetek's U.S. Patent Number 8,240,362'; it maintains a virtual-marking page listing 40 US patents.

strategyRead: 1. **(High confidence)** We assess Ecolab paid for channel position and manufacturing scale rather than for patents, and that the price says so. Basis: 29 times next-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA for a hardware maker whose stated assets are '4 of the top 5 server OEMs and 4 of the 5 hyperscalers as customers', NVIDIA Recommended Vendor List placement, '100s of coolant distribution units … 10,000s of server coldplate loops per month' and a 112,000-square-foot Canadian CDU plant; Ecolab's own thesis names 'deep preexisting relationships with the world's major hyperscaler and colocation customers' first. The Asetek record shows the patents are defensible; nothing in it shows they excluded Vertiv, Motivair, Boyd or the OEMs' in-house lines.

2. **(High confidence)** We assess the coolant distribution unit is where the category's margin and its consolidation are being decided, and that CoolIT is positioned in the leading group but not at its head. Basis: the row CDU moved from 750 kW (CHx750) to 1,500 kW and 2,000 kW within 2025, with a 1 MW-plus-rack unit due 28 September 2026; Dell'Oro counts 'around 40 companies with CDUs' and expects 'fewer than 10 vendors to ultimately capture the lion's share', naming Vertiv as leader and CoolIT among 'established players … maintaining strong market share positions'; Omdia had placed CoolIT first in 2023. The rack-count-per-CDU (12 GB300 NVL72 racks) has become the unit of competition.

3. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess the Ecolab combination is a bet that the recurring revenue of liquid cooling is chemistry and monitoring, not hardware. Basis: Ecolab's stated intent to provide 'a complete cooling solution' from 'water, chemistry and digital service'; CoolIT's six-monthly preventive maintenance with coolant analysis, two-to-five-year SLAs and the post-close bundling of 3D TRASAR monitoring; the field anecdote that a hyperscaler's inadequate flushing clogged filters 'within minutes'; Ecolab's 25-percent operating-margin target for the segment. The risk is that hyperscalers run their own fluid programmes (OCP quarterly testing guidance) and treat the CDU as a commodity.

4. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess CoolIT's customer base is concentrated in a small number of unnamed hyperscalers and that the concentration is undisclosed by design. Basis: 'one large cloud service provider requested thousands of skidded CDUs'; Ecolab's reference to 'major hyperscaler and colocation customers'; no customer in this corpus named by either side; Dell'Oro's note that Aaon's 'deep hyperscaler partnerships and the ability to deliver highly customized solutions can quickly translate into market share gains' — which cuts both ways for an incumbent. Ecolab's segment reporting will not resolve this.

5. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess NVIDIA sets CoolIT's roadmap on both the demand and the specification side, and that the Vera Rubin generation shifts value toward warm-water CDU design and away from the cold plate as the constraint. Basis: every CDU is rated in GB200/GB300 NVL72 racks; the cold-plate demonstrators (4 kW, 15 kW at 45 °C) are aimed at NVIDIA's stated 45 °C supply direction; independent estimates put Rubin racks at 180–220 kW against 120–140 kW for Blackwell; and CoolIT's own January 2026 post argues that 45 °C water 'does not magically eliminate the need for mechanical cooling'. The company has claimed no product for Vera Rubin NVL72 — a gap to watch on 28 September.

6. **(Low confidence)** We assess the OEM channel is more contestable than the '4 of the top 5' phrasing implies. Basis: Supermicro's and Lenovo's own materials describe in-house CDUs and cold plates with no CoolIT mention; Dell lists JetCool as an OEM partner alongside its CoolIT-factory-installed history; HPE's quoted collaboration dates from 2020 and Gigabyte pairs CoolIT with Motivair. Against this: Dell's factory-installed DLC since 2017, the El Capitan and Frontier credits, and the NVIDIA RVL route to every ODM.

7. **(Low confidence)** We assess the two premises the commissioning brief carried — KKR ownership and a 2022 jury verdict — are the kind of errors that propagate through a corpus, and we record the corrections as findings. Basis: Ecolab's SEC-filed release and 10-Q for the ownership; the RECAP-hosted summary-judgment order, the Asetek and CoolIT statements and the Federal Circuit opinions for the litigation. The 'December jury verdict' belongs to Asetek's case against Cooler Master (2014), not to CoolIT.

Collection gap: CoolIT publishes no revenue, margin, installed-megawatt or annual unit figure; the two Asian contract manufacturers are unnamed; CDU weights, heat-exchanger type, input voltage and coolant temperature limits beyond the ASHRAE class are not published; no hyperscaler, colocation or neocloud customer is named by any source; the full KKR 2023 and 2026 releases and CoolIT's own Ecolab announcement were not readable (403/404); Ken Lau has no headshot; the board and reporting line under Ecolab are not disclosed. Note that 'Switch Datacenters', a Dutch operator CoolIT partnered with in 2023, is not the Switch covered in this corpus and no link is recorded.
